decisions.executionNote: Establish elbow-up approach on both sides; aim to collect cameras into the center basket. Initial orientation and reach are being checked.
Approach the left and right cameras with open jaws, keeping the arms on their own sides. Rotate toward downward grasping and inspect alignment before lowering.
Lower onto the two camera bodies and close. Grasp depth is estimated from RGB and link6-to-finger offset; retention will be tested by a lift.
Lift both camera grasps to verify retention. Advance the left camera toward the blue basket while keeping the right camera back for clearance.
Both cameras remain visible between the jaws. Carry the left camera above the left half of blue; stage the right one behind the basket to avoid gripper overlap.
The previous chunk stopped at a continuity guard. Replan with smaller forward increments and lower the left camera over blue, leaving the right grasp staged behind.
Release the left camera inside blue, then clear leftward while bringing the retained right camera toward the right half of the same basket.
Lower the right camera into blue. Move the open left gripper toward the white pen, aligning its jaws across the pen rather than along it.
Open the right gripper to leave its camera in blue and retreat. Lower the left jaws onto the white pen using the estimated finger offset.
Close on and test-lift the white pen with the left arm; lower the right open jaws toward the remaining camera.
White pen retention is uncertain and appears offset from the jaw center; reopen and realign lower. Close the remaining camera and test its retention with a vertical lift.
Regrasp the centered white pen slightly deeper and lift to check it. Carry the visibly retained third camera toward blue with small forward increments.
The white pen slipped and rotated; reopen and realign. The right camera appears at the basket rim, so lift before advancing farther into blue.
Use wrist-image error to shift the left jaws toward the white pen before closing. Advance the third camera slowly above the blue basket while preserving configuration continuity.
Replan after the right IK guard: lower first to reduce folding, then use tiny forward motion. Center the white pen in the left jaws, close, and test-lift.
The previous action executed nothing. Reduce the initial right lowering increment to one millimeter to satisfy continuity, while retrying the left pen grasp.
The white pen is now visibly between closed jaws; lift and carry it toward white. Bring the third camera farther inside blue with small coupled forward/downward increments.
Release the third camera in blue and withdraw the right arm. The pen fell during transport; realign the left wrist across its new horizontal orientation for a deeper grasp.
Replan after the five-step prefix: withdraw the right gripper with reduced increments and continue the left pen approach, checking the new jaw alignment.
Left tracking indicates contact with the white basket, not the pen. Back away and make the grasp more vertical before lowering. Move the right open gripper toward the white toy.
Lower the left jaws around the pen, clear of the basket rim. Align the right jaws around the white toy's torso rather than its head.
Close both grasps without further downward pressure, then test retention with short vertical lifts; the pen is close to the basket wall.
Neither object is retained. Use a narrower pen approach to avoid the basket wall, and move the right grasp forward and deeper around the toy's body.
Close on the newly centered pen and toy, then lift only a few centimeters to check for retention before transport.
The toy may be pinched near its foot; test further lift before reaching red. Move the left grasp toward the pen's visible end and close below it, avoiding the basket wall.
The toy fell rather than remaining pinched. Reopen and lower over its new torso location. Shift the left grip farther along the exposed pen end to avoid basket contact.
The pen now spans the jaw center. Close it; correct the right torso grasp laterally before closing and testing both with a short lift.
Both objects now appear centered between the closed fingers. Lift vertically to clear the basket rims and verify that neither slips before transport.
Both objects remained fixed in the wrist views during lifting. Carry the white pen above white and the white toy above red, keeping both grips closed.
Lower the retained pen into white and the toy into red, then open both grippers to release them within their respective basket boundaries.
Both released objects are inside their baskets. Withdraw and reorient for the remaining central pen and dark toy; use inward-facing tools while keeping arm links on their own sides.
Approach the dark toy from the right with an inward-facing gripper; keep the left arm staged back while completing its pen-grasp orientation.
Lower the right inward-facing jaws around the dark toy's torso. Keep the left gripper stationary and separated until the toy is lifted clear.
Clear the left gripper away from the right approach. Settle the right jaws slightly deeper around the dark toy, close, and perform a small retention lift.
The dark toy was not retained. Reopen and lower the right grasp to engage the torso sides more deeply, then close without transporting.
The dark toy now lies between the right fingers. Lift vertically, then slightly outward, to test retention and clear the center before transporting.
The toy slipped out near its feet. Reopen and approach farther along its torso for a more secure pinch; withdraw the unused left arm for clearance.
Close the right jaws around the centered torso and test with a slow lift. Stage the left arm nearer the remaining pen, still behind the right grasp.
The dark toy is not securely retained. Reopen and move the right jaws farther onto the torso at table height. Advance the left pen approach while keeping it behind the toy.
The toy rolled to one side of the open jaws. Shift the right grasp laterally toward the visible torso with a slight upward clearance, then close.
Test the right toy grasp with a lift and slight outward motion. Reorient the left jaws across the black pen and stage above it without crossing the arms.
The toy is still on the table. Separate the arms by withdrawing the right side, and lower the left gripper onto the black pen from its own workspace.
Center the black pen between the left fingers using its wrist-image offset, lower to its sides, and close. Keep the right arm clear.
Test the black pen grasp with a gentle upward lift, then shift left to clear the center. Keep the gripper fully closed during retention testing.
The pen remained on the table after lifting. Reopen and retry a deeper, slightly shifted grasp to put the narrow shaft between the finger pads, keeping link6 on the left side.
Center the pen shaft with a small lateral correction, close at the deeper height, and test retention with a two-centimeter lift.
Lift the centered pen grasp and move left slowly, keeping the jaws closed. Check that the shaft moves with the wrist before carrying it to white.
The previous pinch was near the pen tip and did not retain it. Flatten the left approach to reach farther along the shaft while keeping link6 on the left side.
The shaft is now within reach rather than just the point. Lower the finger pads to pen height, close, and make a short test lift.
The black shaft is now visibly pinched between the pads. Lift and shift left gently, keeping the gripper closed, to verify stable retention.
The pen stayed fixed between the pads during the lift. Carry it leftward toward the white basket at rim-clearing height, maintaining its current orientation.
Center the retained black pen above white before release. With the center unobstructed, bring the right arm toward the dark toy's newly visible torso.
The pen slipped outside white at the rim. Retreat and reorient the left gripper for a more vertical regrasp. Bring the right jaws over the dark toy with small increments.
Change the right approach to a steeper grasp with jaws across the toy's torso, not along its length. Move the left open jaws above the pen's new position.
Finish aligning the right jaws across the toy and lower onto its torso. Center the left fingers on the relocated pen and descend for a vertical grasp.
Close and lift the centered pen. The right fingers are around the toy's head rather than torso; lift slightly, shift toward the body, and lower again with the jaws open.
The pen did not rise with the wrist; reopen and target the middle shaft deeper. Correct the right torso alignment slightly, close, and test with a short lift.
Close around the pen's centered shaft and test a vertical lift. Reopen the right jaws and engage the dark toy's torso more deeply before closing again.
Both objects now appear between the finger pads. Lift vertically with closed jaws to verify retention and gain clearance before moving toward the baskets.
The pen remains stable; carry it above white at clearance height. The toy is retained but hanging, so lift further while moving outward toward red before advancing over its rim.
Advance and lower the pen within white. Carry the hanging toy forward above red at its current safe height; keep both grasps closed until fully over the baskets.
Release the pen inside white and withdraw. After the right IK interruption, use smaller coupled forward/downward increments to bring the hanging toy safely inside red.
Withdraw the open left gripper so the pen can settle. Tilt the right grasp forward and advance slowly to move the hanging toy past red's front rim before release.
Release the dark toy inside red, pause for settling, and withdraw the right hand. Bring the open left arm toward its origin while monitoring the upright pen.
Both categories' remaining objects are inside their assigned baskets. Return the left arm to origin and withdraw the right arm with open grippers, allowing the objects to settle.
Continue the right arm's elbow-up return toward origin; hold the left arm at origin with both grippers open. The black pen remains upright inside white.
